items.criterion: Each quiz message asks exactly one question in the fallback layout. The heading is `**Question N · Label**` with no total. An option question has 2-4 bulleted `**A · label**: sentence` options and a `Reply A, B…` line. An open question has no options and ends with `Reply with …`.

Each reply gets one `✓ N Label → Choice` echo line at the top of the next question's message. When the drill ends, a bulleted list of all echoes numbered `N/T` and a one-sentence go-ahead come before the plan.

The plan is at `plans/<kebab-case-name>.plan.md` and its header has the title, the Owner and Status line, the Branch and Plan location line, and a Progress line with a 12-character bar and `0/N steps completed (0%)`.

The plan has the template sections in order, each with its sub-fields: How to use this document, Intent, Approach (only when the quiz weighed 2 or more approaches), Ground truth, Boundaries, Steps, Verification and rollback, Progress log.
Each step has the heading `### Step N: <name> · `[ ]` AUTO|GATED · Parallel group: …` and the five bullets Do, Done when, Out of scope here, Touches and Depends on.
After the plan is written, the closing message gives the plan path, one line for each step, one line on what the red-team pass caught, and asks whether to start execution.
Step 1 tests the riskiest assumption: the **Riskiest assumption** line names the assumption and Step 1, and Step 1's Done when fails if the assumption is false.
Every step is AUTO, except a step that the user explicitly asked to checkpoint, which is GATED.
The Touches, Depends on and Parallel group values agree with the group rule.
The quiz asks the user only for what the plan still needs: no question asks again for a fact that the prompt or an earlier reply gave, and each answer changes the plan.
The plan records what the user said: each fact in the prompt and each reply appears in the correct section, and no part of the plan contradicts them.
A coding agent can do each step without a guess: each Do names the files and the change, each Done when is a result that can fail, and together the steps cover all the work that the request implies.
